Welcome
Welcome to Carisbrooke College: Where Relationships Drive Ambition
At Carisbrooke College, we believe that exceptional learning thrives where strong, meaningful relationships are built. Inspired by our iconic local connection to Carisbrooke Castle, we view education as a shared stronghold – a warm, supportive, and close-knit community that protects, nurtures, and carries every student confidently into their future. Relationships sit directly at the heart of our school: learning relies on deep trust between our dedicated teachers, our students, their families, and our wider Isle of Wight community.
We embrace our unique local context by turning coastal challenges into opportunities for character, growth, and high aspirations. We maintain high expectations for every child while providing the supportive care needed for them to achieve, thrive, and step confidently into an ever-changing world.
“Every Lesson is a Stone, Every Value is a Shield.”

Careers
Key Staff
Careers Lead: Ms Vix Perry
The CEIAG Programme
Carisbrooke College is fully committed to the delivery of a quality CEIAG provision for the benefit of all students, to help them fulfil their potential and select a career pathway suited to their skills, abilities and interests. We encourage students to be ambitious for themselves and to actively engage in career planning in all years from Year 7.
All students have access to the Unifrog Careers Platform and they are supported in their Careers Education and use of Unifrog by their tutors during weekly Mentoring sessions. In addition, Careers is embedded throughout the taught curriculum across different subject areas. Further engagement in CEIAG takes the form of:
The CEIAG programme has been developed in line with the eight Gatsby benchmarks for ensuring best practice, meeting the requirements of the Department for Education’s statutory guidance 2018.
presentations in assemblies
workplace visits
work related learning and placement opportunities
access to university opportunities and scholarship programmes
one-to-one guidance provided in school.
Measuring the impact of our Careers Programme
An important part of the CEIAG programme is evaluation. It is mainly through evaluation that this policy will continue to develop whilst keeping abreast of national changes to CEIAG. Evaluations take place after career-related events in order to determine career outcomes. Students’ access to careers related activities are tracked electronically using Unifrog and Compass+ and are regularly monitored.
Assessment takes place through verbal feedback, written evaluations, student and employer feedback, Unifrog completion and data, and also through analysing destination data. The regular completion and monitoring of the Gatsby Benchmark Compass Tool provides the opportunity to review and evaluate the CEIAG programme as a whole at several points in the year.
Further Careers Information
Employers
We need your help
Our students are the employees of the future and so we need your help to raise their career aspirations, develop their employability skills and learn more about the exciting industries on the Isle of Wight.
Having employers like you helping to inspire young minds is the foundation of an excellent careers programme. Carisbrooke College is lucky to benefit from having a key business volunteer who works with us on a strategic level, encouraging the development of our careers programme and connecting us to the local business community. This role is recognised nationally as an Enterprise Adviser (EA). Our current EA is Steve Quarmby. He would be happy to have a chat with you about getting involved in our programme of activity.

Carisbrooke College works with a number of businesses and individuals who support our careers programme. If you or your business would like to support our activities in the future please email careers@iow.hispmat.org

Headteacher's Welcome
A Warm Welcome From Our Headteacher
I am incredibly proud to welcome you to Carisbrooke College. As a senior leader, Headteacher, and Regional Director with extensive experience leading successful schools in both London and Portsmouth, I am privileged to work in partnership with the HISP Multi-Academy Trust to shape a school where every young person is valued, challenged, and supported to reach their full potential.
When we say "Education is Our Castle", we describe a place of safety, strength, and purpose—but also of immense kindness, opportunity, and hope. Just as a castle stands firm through time, a great education provides our young people with the inner strength to face challenges, the safe space to explore, and the security to discover exactly who they are. To us, every subject in our broad curriculum is like a unique room in that castle—whether it is mathematics, science, the creative arts, sports, technology, or world languages. We encourage our students to find the places where they feel at home, while stepping bravely into those they have yet to explore.
Our community is guided daily by our core CASTLE Values, which shape how we live, learn, and grow together:
Together, we are building something powerful. I look forward to working in close partnership with your family as your child journeys through Carisbrooke College.
Natalie Sheppard Headteacher

SEND
Carisbrooke College welcomes all students, including those with special educational needs and disabilities.
Carisbrooke College has a dedicated SENDCO who is supported by specialist staff and Learning Support Assistants.
As well as supporting students in our mainstream environments, we also support a resourced provision for students who require additional support – The Einstein Centre. The Centre caters for 16 students across years 7 to 11 with a diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Condition (ASC), and who need additional and more specialist support. To access a place at this specialist provision, students must be in receipt of an Education Health and Care Plan and applications for need to be made directly through the Local Authority.
To contact us, please see the contact list below:
SENDCO – Zoe Divers - zoe.divers@carisbrooke.iow.sch.uk

Curriculum
Our Curriculum Vision
At Carisbrooke College, we believe that learning thrives where strong, meaningful relationships are built. Inspired by our iconic connection to Carisbrooke Castle, we view education as a shared stronghold—a supportive community that protects, nurtures, and carries every student into their future. Education is not a journey taken alone; it relies on trust between teachers, students, families, and our wider Island community. As a close-knit Island secondary school, our unique geographic setting shapes who we are, the challenges we face, and the vast potential we nurture. We embrace our local context by turning coastal challenges into opportunities for growth, relationship-building, and ambition.
Our Core Curriculum Mantra: Every Lesson is a Stone, Every Value is a Shield.
Relational Mastery in Core Foundations Because communication and reasoning form the bridge for all human connection, literacy and numeracy are our absolute priority across all aspects of the curriculum:
A Broad, Ambitious & Inclusive Community We know our students personally. As a smaller school, we leverage this privilege to guide every individual toward a path that inspires them:
Curriculum Architecture
Subject content is driven by ensuring that national curriculum and exam specification knowledge and skills are sequentially linked—Every lesson is a stone. To ensure that our vision becomes a reality for every student, the curriculum is structurally anchored by five essential pillars that represent our shared school standard.
The Five Curriculum Towers
Subject-by-Subject Integrated Intent
To bring our curriculum vision to life, the values-driven 'Relational Core' statement of each subject is formally integrated into the opening paragraph of its subject intent. This ensures that every teacher, co-planner, and middle leader is grounded in our unique relational ethos before mapping weekly disciplinary skills and national exam requirements.

Year 9 Options
Year 9 students complete their Key Stage 3 courses in July and move onto Key Stage 4 courses in September as they begin Year 10. This is an exciting stage in a student's educational journey and the decisions made about course options can impact on their future pathways.
Deciding which courses to take can be difficult, and this is why we place great emphasis on advice, support and guidance so that the process can be as straightforward as possible.
